status: design-only; no source/cache/repository edits, build, or tests

currentNativeFacts.rule: Add replaces the last active shield with equal (Type, ShieldTarget). It calls old.OnOverwrite before assigning new, then emits OnShielded for new. No OnExpire or OnShieldBreak on replacement.

OnDamage visits each applicable shield; an OnDamage return of false drops that exact object, and OnShieldBreak is emitted after compaction. Shield-specific OnDamage can queue damage before handler removal.
Tick expires only if shield.Expiry() == current frame; calls OnExpire before removal, then emits OnShieldBreak. It does not call OnOverwrite.
Core.Tick runs Player.Tick, including Shields.Tick, before Core.Tasks.Run in the same global frame. This order matters at an expiry/task boundary.

ShieldOwner/Target/Type are semantic fields. Tmpl.Key() returns Src frame, which is not unique among same-frame shield instances. SourceHostHPID is mutable: Tmpl.OnDamage via Bridge.ShieldDamage replaces it with the latest HP calculation ID.

Current sourcehost captures player-shield HP arithmetic/provenance and a live phase snapshot. It does not emit shield instance birth/replacement/break/expiry, active owner, or terminal callback receipts; custom shield private state remains a phase coverage gap.
Shield interface exposes OnDamage, OnExpire and OnOverwrite separately, so a generic OnShieldBreak event alone cannot distinguish expiry from damage break.

laneDifference.classic: newShield does not set Tmpl.Ele, leaving the native enum zero value.
laneDifference.implication: Shield absorption/break behavior may differ by lane; do not collapse the two into a single inferred survival schedule. Stellar Noelle likewise explicitly sets Geo while classic leaves its constructor element unset.

minimalObservationAPI.principle: All receipts are read-only observations of actual native events. Do not replace a shield hook, infer termination by elapsed time, or use Src frame as identity.
minimalObservationAPI.handlerHook: Add an optional sourcehost lifecycle observer on shield.Handler. It receives exact Shield object at Add/OnDamage/Tick branches and brackets the existing OnOverwrite, OnDamage, OnExpire callbacks without changing order, arguments, return values or emitted events.
minimalObservationAPI.instanceIdentity: Assign monotonically increasing simulation-local shieldInstanceId for every actual Add object; retain identity for that object through replacement/break/expiry and keep a separate birth HP calculation ID. Internal pointer identity may be used only to look up the assigned ID; never expose addresses. If a shield implementation cannot be keyed safely, expose an explicit coverage gap.

shieldInstancesRow.replacesInstanceId: optional positive int when Handler.Add matches type+target
shieldInstancesRow.terminalReason: overwritten | broken | expired; absent while active

shieldTransitionsRow.kind: added | overwrite-hook | damage-hook | broken | expire-hook | expired | shielded-event | shield-break-event
shieldTransitionsRow.playerAttackId: optional positive int for damage branch

minimalObservationAPI.effectContext: While invoking exact OnDamage/OnExpire/OnOverwrite of an instance, Bridge records active shieldInstanceId and hook cause; Restore after callback. Attack CaptureAttack receives this private owner plus source-site ID only when audited character source emits. Handler.Emit events retain original order. For direct refresh attack before Handler.Add, source code must explicitly bind the old `exist` shield object; generic OnOverwrite context cannot see this attack.
minimalObservationAPI.phaseState: Expose live shieldInstanceId and terminal relation in SourceHostPhaseState; retain current HP/relative expiry and separate existing SourceHostHPID mutable provenance. Custom implementation private-state gaps remain unless reviewed, not blanket promoted.

xinyan.skill: E queues one direct initial attack at skillHitmark 15. Each actual enemy-hit callback increments hitOpponents and schedules a character task to update shield level at a hitlag-sensitive time. If no XinyanSkill shield existed at cast time, a separate level-1 creation task is registered. A1 lowers level2/3 opponent-count thresholds. Level3 update starts the recurring shieldDot task and replaces the shield object.
xinyan.burstC2: Q at C2+ queues two additional direct shield-pulse attacks at c2PulseHitmarks in addition to initial physical hit and seven Q Pyro hits. A hitlag-sensitive character task at burstShieldStart 43 updates to level3 and starts shieldDot; C0-C1 has no Q-created shield. The two pulses are direct Q roots, not shieldDot emissions.
xinyan.shieldHooks: xinyanShield.OnExpire and broken OnDamage reset c.shieldLevel=1; inherited OnOverwrite is a no-op. Replacement does not run OnExpire/OnShieldBreak.
xinyan.dotGate: Each shieldDot task checks Get(XinyanSkill)!=nil, c.shieldLevel==3 and c.shieldTickSrc==captured src. It queues exactly one attack then one next task only when all three pass. The src is a frame, not a shield instance ID. An old task could pass under a newer shield if updates share a frame; record both task-chain owner and actual gate shieldInstanceId, never silently reassign ownership to the new object.
requiredProducerSites: xinyan.skill.hit-to-shield-update (callback-owned character task; may update level2/3)
xinyan.skill.initial-level1 (non-damage task proving possible shield creation)
xinyan.closure: Use actual callback batches/hit count, shield transitions and task producer receipts. DoT chain closes only after its observed terminal task (gate failed) or an explicit cancellation receipt; a pending future task blocks complete scope. Do not presume 12-second shield expiry alone proves all ticks or fixed count. Same-frame replacement and concurrent E/Q require actual chain + gate identity receipts.
xinyan.sourceLimit: Current 108 ability producer helper only links registrations within an active invocation or producer. E hit callback schedules update task after Skill returned; it needs 111 callback-owned task registration linkage (not a heuristic creation-action ancestry) before E-shield DoT can be a complete intrinsic cast.

baizhu.burstTasks: Q registers exactly six Core tasks: first shield at frame offset81 and five refresh tasks at offsets81+142+146*i, i=0..4. These tasks create new shield objects; five refresh tasks also directly call healing after summon. At summonSeamlessShield, if any BaizhuBurst shield exists, summonSpiritvein queues one attack before the new shield is added; then Handler.Add replaces old shield through inherited no-op OnOverwrite.
baizhu.breakAndExpiry: Baizhu shield OnDamage calls removeShield (heal + Spiritvein queue) when HP reaches zero. OnExpire calls the same. These happen before Handler removes the shield. A given actual shield instance can terminate by break, expiry or replacement; each observed reason must be distinct. No fixed Spiritvein total is valid without observing breaks, refreshes, C6 insertion and horizon.
baizhu.c6: C6 makeC6CB creates a Seamless Shield on its first executed sprite hit callback. In pinned skill.go it is attached to the first Skill attack when chain callback is present; in cons.go it is attached to the C2 Splice attack. The C6-created shield can overwrite a Q shield, and a later Q refresh can overwrite that C6 shield. It is a separate callback-origin creation, not automatically owned by the Q invocation.
requiredProducerSites: baizhu.c6.sprite-shield (audited hit callback site, only when actual callback executes)
baizhu.shield.spiritvein (attack emit site with consumed existing shieldInstanceId and explicit cause: refresh, break, expiry)
baizhu.ownerRule: Refresh Spiritvein is tied to the exact old `exist` shield, by explicit source wrapper around the call before Add. Break/expiry Spiritvein is tied to the exact current shield in Handler callback context. Every new shield carries its own creation origin/site, replacement relation and terminal reason. The Q action may create a new Q shield while consuming an old C6 shield; do not count that old C6 Spiritvein as a Q-owned shield emission merely because a Q task triggered replacement.
baizhu.closure: For standalone Q, all six Q creation tasks must complete, every resulting Q-owned shield must have an observed terminal relation, all old-shield Spiritvein emits attributable by instance must dispatch to terminal target outcomes, and any C6/external shield interleaving must remain separately identified. Do not infer final shield expiry from its configured 152-frame lifetime; observation must reach actual native Tick or break/replacement. If a C6 callback is pending, keep dependent shield scope partial.

reuseInventory.benefit: Replacement computes capped stacked/refresh HP from old shield and previous SourceHostHPSource; instance relation plus stable birth and mutable HP provenance makes refresh trace auditable.
OnExpire/OnDamage reset shielded/A1 tags; refresh replacement does not invoke those hooks. Instance reason receipts prevent false tag-reset assumptions.
OnOverwrite, OnExpire, and broken OnDamage each call explodeShield; demonstrates why all three hook contexts must be captured separately.
Break/expiry may trigger character-specific effects or regeneration tasks. Generic lifecycle receipt can report cause without assuming their gameplay formulas.

notYetProven: No native runtime receipts have been collected for the proposed API.
No claim of real-game shield timing or damage frequency is made; these are pinned simulator paths.
Character callbacks and task chains require source-site annotations before a finite-cast complete verdict; lifecycle events alone cannot close them.
